description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/README.md:23-38

CURRENT BLOCK:
    \`\`\`rust
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use jmap_contacts_server::{ContactsBackend, register_contacts_handlers};
    use jmap_server::Dispatcher;

    // 1. Implement ContactsBackend for your storage layer (see trait section below).
    struct MyBackend { /* db pool, etc. */ }
    impl ContactsBackend for MyBackend { /* ... */ }

    // 2. Wire all 9 contacts methods into a Dispatcher in one call.
    let mut dispatcher: Dispatcher<()> = Dispatcher::new();
    register_contacts_handlers(&mut dispatcher, Arc::new(MyBackend { /* ... */ }));
    \`\`\`

PROBLEM:
This block is the FIRST thing a new caller reads after the elevator
pitch. It is the de-facto contract example. It does NOT compile, for
multiple reasons:

1. **`impl ContactsBackend for MyBackend { /* ... */ }` is incomplete.**
   ContactsBackend is a subtrait of JmapBackend; the impl block must
   provide every required JmapBackend method (account_exists,
   get_objects, get_state, get_changes, query_objects, query_changes)
   plus every required ContactsBackend method (create_object,
   update_object, destroy_object, supports_type, copy_contact_card,
   address_book_has_contents). The example shows none of them.

2. **type Error / type CallerCtx missing.** JmapBackend's two
   associated types are required and not shown.

3. **`Dispatcher<()>` vs `B::CallerCtx` mismatch implicit.** The
   `Dispatcher<()>` constructor requires that `MyBackend::CallerCtx
   = ()`. The reader does not see that constraint until they hit a
   compile error.

4. **`Arc::new(MyBackend { /* ... */ })` is `Arc<MyBackend>` not
   `Arc<dyn ...>`.** This part is OK as-is, but combined with #3 the
   error message will mention CallerCtx without explanation.

A reader who copy-pastes this sample gets a wall of trait-impl errors
on the very first build. The code sample serves the OPPOSITE purpose
of its intended role: it actively misleads about the surface area
required to implement a ContactsBackend.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
That the README's How-to-use example is a working starting point.

RECOMMENDED:
Replace with a documented, doctest-able example. The lib.rs already
contains the right shape (lib.rs:9-17):

    \`\`\`rust,no_run
    # use std::sync::Arc;
    # use jmap_contacts_server::{ContactsBackend, register_contacts_handlers};
    # use jmap_server::Dispatcher;
    # fn example<B: ContactsBackend<CallerCtx = ()> + 'static>(backend: B) {
    let mut dispatcher: Dispatcher<()> = Dispatcher::new();
    register_contacts_handlers(&mut dispatcher, Arc::new(backend));
    # }
    \`\`\`

That doctest IS already in lib.rs and presumably passes `cargo test
--doc`. Copy the same idiom into the README so the rendered docs at
crates.io/docs.rs and the README match.

Alternative: link the README to the `lib.rs` rustdoc:
    "For a complete working example, see [the crate docs]."

P1 because the README is the primary discovery surface for new
consumers and the broken example will produce confused issue traffic
the moment this crate publishes.

PARENT EPIC RELATIONSHIP: this is orthogonal to JMAP-qz9v.1 (README
documents an unimplemented cascade); both are README-as-contract
findings but on different sections.
title: README §'How to use' code sample does not compile — missing JmapBackend supertrait methods, type Error, type CallerCtx
